core.title: Use kebab-case for logical identifiers and snake_case for plan filesystem names
core.given: A planner writes a logical identifier (any URN, slug field or reference in the profile's reference syntax, in any file) or a plan filesystem artifact (a wagon's plan directory, its manifest file, or a feature file)
core.when: The planner writes or edits the identifier, or creates or renames the path
core.then: Write logical identifiers (URNs, slug fields, references in the profile's reference syntax) in kebab-case, and name plan filesystem artifacts in snake_case at the locations and with the name patterns the profile gives for plan artifacts: the wagon directory under the plan root, the wagon manifest named after that directory (not after the logical slug), and feature files under the wagon directory.
prefer: Keep the logical-to-physical mapping consistent: name each wagon directory, manifest and feature file after its entity's logical identifier, case-converted per this rule and the profile's plan layout
Name the wagon manifest after its directory, not after the logical slug
avoid: Hyphenated plan directory or feature file names copied from the hyphenated logical identifier
Underscored values in any URN, slug field or reference in the profile's reference syntax
Naming the wagon manifest after the logical slug instead of its directory
core.why: Consistent filesystem naming reduces conversion complexity and keeps logical (kebab) and physical (snake) identifiers clearly separate.
evidence: Every wagon directory directly under the plan root is snake_case and contains a manifest named after that directory per the profile's plan-artifact name pattern
Every feature file under a wagon's plan directory has a snake_case name
Every URN, slug field and reference in the profile's reference syntax, in any file and for any entity type, is kebab-case
verification: Check naming by surface: logical-identifier surfaces (URNs, slug fields, references in the profile's reference syntax) must be kebab-case in any file; plan filesystem surfaces (wagon directories, manifest files, feature files) must be snake_case at the profile's plan locations and name patterns; either surface alone is a finding.

Normalization: the expected wagon directory name is the logical slug with hyphens replaced by underscores (kebab-to-snake), and the manifest filename must equal the profile's manifest name pattern applied to that directory name (the manifest matches the directory, not the slug). The full slug-to-directory-name conversion is owned by the separate naming-conversion rule and is not asserted here.

Enforcement needs a diff-level observer (needs_new_observer) that detects any URN, slug or reference value in the profile's reference syntax added or changed in any file regardless of the entity it names, and any plan directory or file created or renamed; either change activates the check.

Scope: the filesystem branch applies recursively under the plan root (directories, manifests and feature files anywhere under it); the logical-identifier branch is not gated by the plan tree and is not limited to any entity type, so files outside the plan tree are checked only for URNs, slug fields and references in the profile's reference syntax.
The task terms (urn, slug, ref, wagon, feature, manifest) are supporting activation signals only, not gates.

fires: The planner creates a new wagon directory under the plan root together with its manifest
The planner adds a feature file under a wagon's plan directory
The planner writes or edits any URN, slug field or reference in the profile's reference syntax, in any file, inside or outside the plan tree, whatever entity it names
The planner renames an entity, so both its slug and its plan path change
doesNotFire: Edits to the body of an existing plan artifact that change no URNs, slugs, references, filenames or directory names
Changes to files outside the plan tree that add or change no URNs, slug fields or references in the profile's reference syntax

profileRequirements.meaning: Root tree of plan artifacts. The filesystem branch of this rule applies recursively under this root; the logical-identifier branch may reach files outside it.
Where one wagon's plan directory sits; these directory names must be snake_case and hold the wagon manifest.
Name pattern of plan-artifact files; here the wagon manifest, whose name must be derived from its directory name (not from the logical slug).
Path of a feature's plan file under the plan root; defines the feature file's location and snake_case name pattern.
The stack's concrete plan-artifact kinds (wagon manifest, feature file, plan markup) for the file_kind activation fact.

The reference surface: the syntax by which any file holds a reference value. It is the third logical-identifier surface this rule checks for kebab-case, in any file and for any entity type; for Bun it instantiates to YAML references.
profileRequirements.bunValue: YAML ref (references are YAML reference values, in any file)

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's concrete syntax for reference values: how any file holds a reference to another artifact. Cores that check logical-identifier casing use this surface instead of naming a data language.
proposedKeys.bunValue: YAML ref (references are YAML reference values, in any file)
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The idiom group covers handlers, gates, markup kinds and other constructs, and urn.binding covers only how a source file binds to a URN; no key states which reference surface (e.g. YAML refs) a logical-identifier rule must check.

neutralityNotes: Fixes from the round-2 feedback: (1) the third logical-identifier surface is no longer generalized to all references; the core says 'reference in the profile's reference syntax' and the surface is profile data via the proposed idiom.reference_syntax key (Bun: YAML refs), used consistently in given, then, avoid[1], evidence[2], verification and the fires/change/doesNotFire activation text, so a non-YAML reference that is neither a URN nor a slug field is out of scope exactly as in bun.json. (2) The generic kebab-to-snake normalization (hyphens replaced by underscores) now lives in core:verification with the original qualification that the full slug-to-directory conversion is owned by the separate naming-conversion rule; only the concrete manifest name pattern remains profile data (suffix.plan_artifact), so verifier_detail[1] is no longer bunOnly. (3) roots.plan bunValue is the root path 'plan'; the recursive filesystem scope is expressed in core:verification instead of a scan glob. Residuals: the concrete plan path and name patterns are profile data (roots.plan, layout.wagon_dir, suffix.plan_artifact, layout.plan_item), not core text; the path_glob activation fact has no counterpart in the closed neutral fact vocabulary and is re-expressed as a plan_artifact role fact plus the plan-root key with branch semantics in fires/doesNotFire and verification (raw form kept bunOnly); kebab-case and snake_case are treated as stack-neutral naming conventions; 'wagon' is used only as the profile-vocabulary concept behind layout.wagon_dir. bun.json declares no per-rule severity or disposition, so verification carries only the generic check description, normalization, scope and observer needs; detector/validator/finding ids are not present in this rule's sidecar.
